text:
Maria: kicking off a short design check: proposing an "adaptive admission taper" to smooth spikes without hard token evictions. sketching config + rollout plan, want quick gut-checks.
AJ: sounds promising. how's this different from reservoirs or grace pools?
Maria: tapering applies a probabilistic taper per-tenant based on short-term token surge, with a small hedged-pass to avoid tail misses. reservoirs are bucketed and can be gamed by clients.
Kevin: important: make sure abuse signals still have precedence. We can't let tapering override probation.
Maria: agreed. flow: compute effective_priority = base_priority * (1 - abuse_factor); then apply taper_prob(t) derived from recent token rate. taper never charges tokens, only affects admit probability.
Sarah: telemetry needs: per-tenant recent_rate histogram, taper_applied_ratio, p50/p95 admit latency, and cache_miss_rate when we downshift models.
Nick: rollout: canary 0.5%, then 2%, 10%, 25%. automatic rollback if p95 total latency increases > 8% or error rate > 0.15% for 10m.
Maria: draft policy (pseudo-config):
```
admission:
  mode: taper
  lookback_ms: 12000
  taper_slope: 0.5    # controls aggressiveness
  hedged_pass_ratio: 0.01
  per_tenant_cap: 0.05
  min_request_tokens: 32
  fallback_threshold: 0.9  # use reservoir above this
```
AJ: hedged_pass should be per-tenant and capped; also ensure random seed isolation so sampling isn't correlated across replicas.
Maria: good catch. will add tenant-scoped rng seed and upper/lower bounds.
Kevin: routing concern: if taper denies, we sometimes fallback to smaller model. that can cause kv-cache warming and spike latency later. prefer cache-aware fallback: only downshift if cache affinity exists or cold-warm penalty acceptable.
Nick: add a "cache-warm penalty" metric in canary using synthetic replays of conversations to quantify.
Sarah: ops: add runbook entries to opt-out taper for tenants, command to check taper_applied_ratio, and pager play for token p95 spike. include instructions to view ICS traces and per-route counts.
Maria: compatibility: taper runs upstream of quota engine; quota accounting unchanged. taper only changes short-term acceptance.
AJ: abuse evasion vector: a client could do many mini-bursts to avoid lookback. plan to detect spike patterns across multiple lookbacks and escalate to probation with extended taper.
Kevin: propose a classifier: if a tenant has > N windows with top-k percentile spikes in M minutes, escalate to "probation_taper" with longer decay and lower hedged_pass.
Maria: will add synthetic test suite that includes mimic burst-evasion sequences and run nightly against staging. also add telemetry alert for pattern matches.
rls-bot: scheduled deploy: canary 0.5% Tue 10:30 UTC unless objections.
Nick: i'll own the synthetic harness and seed data; will push by EOD Monday.
Sarah: i'll draft runbook and rollback checklist and a short postmortem template if we need to revert.
AJ: please put config, test harness, and runbook in one PR so SRE + PM can review together.
Maria: will open PR with config, tests, runbook links. thanks all :thumbsup:
Kevin: thumbs. ping me for fairness sim across models.
